### 1. The question, frozen

The title and opening chapter make one question central: **why may Time be treated as a fourth dimension of Space, so that a body could be moved along it — and why has that gone unnoticed?** Kind: forward (what would produce travel through Time), with a backward tail (what the machine's vanishing lets us tell). Range: "any real body"; the demonstration covers one evening, one room. Asked: whether travel in Time is possible, and whether the vanishing shows it. The later questions (the Eloi, the guests' doubt) are answered by later chapters; I leave them out.

### 2. The jobs, and the parts

**Jobs.** J1 why Time is a dimension, not just a measure of change *(given)*. J2 why we draw an unreal distinction between Time and Space *(given)*. J3 why we cannot move freely in Time — yet might by machine *(given)*. J4 why the model vanished *(given)*. J5 why we did not see it in the past *(added, by the narrator)*. J6 why a time-flying machine cannot be seen *(added, by the Psychologist)*.

**Parts**, in the owner's words: **P1** abstractions — "a mathematical line… a cube [of no duration]… have no real existence". **P2** "any real body must have extension in four directions… Length, Breadth, Thickness, and Duration". **P3** "our consciousness moves intermittently in one direction along [Time]". **P4** "no difference between Time and any of the three dimensions of Space except that our consciousness moves along it". **P5** the barometer trace, "along the Time-Dimension". **P6** gravitation limits up and down; balloons overcame it — "why should he not… travel the other way?" **P7** the machine's two levers, "gliding into the future… and this other reverses". **P8** the vanishing — "became indistinct… and it was gone". **P9** "diluted presentation". **P10** "I can't argue tonight… you must refrain from interruptions". **P11** the Eloi.

### 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Held, or loose, by |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Borrowed** | rests on an unexamined claim about mathematical objects existing or not |
| P2 | **Two routes** | with P5, to J1; note its "Duration" detail is itself swappable |
| P3 | **Held if** | only by J2, which is the very thing in doubt |
| P4 | **Loose** | any exception would serve ("except that we remember it") |
| P5 | **Two routes** | with P2, to J1 — the weaker route, since a graph's axes are chosen |
| P6 | **Held** | by J3; but it pulls against P4 (below) |
| P7 | **Loose** | a free design choice; any two controls would do |
| P8 | **Held if** | only by J4, which is in doubt |
| P9 | **Loose** | a catch-all with no gauge (below) |
| P10 | **Fixed** | the owner puts the claim outside argument, and says so |
| P11 | **Borrowed** | rests on an evolutionary account not tested here |

Provenance: P1–P6 are **built** (worked out as geometry and analogy, and criticised by the hearers as he goes); P7–P9 are **asserted**; P8 is **fitted** — tuned on one demonstration that has met no second case.

### 4. Whole-explanation checks

**The answer is hidden in the starting points.** P2 looks like a derived conclusion, but "extension in Duration" just means "lasts". Swap the word: every real body "must have extension in Length, Breadth, Thickness, and Mass" — and the sentence runs just as well. The same steps would "prove" mass a dimension. So the steps are not what hold the conclusion up. P4 does the same work: the conclusion sits inside the clause "except that our consciousness moves along it".

**Direction.** The vanishing was produced by pressing a lever; from the vanishing he concludes travel. Poke the cause (press the lever) and the effect follows. Poke the effect — a conjuring trick also makes a machine vanish — and the cause need not. So the demonstration answers *what we can tell from what we see*, not *what produces it*.

**Flip.** Had the machine stayed put, would the same parts have covered that? Yes: "diluted presentation", or a model not yet working. A history that fits both outcomes is held by neither.

**Pairs that pull.** P4 ("no difference… except consciousness") against P6 (a real obstacle, gravitation, limits our freedom in a Space dimension). If obstacles limit freedom, freedom in Time should have to overcome one too; P4 denies any such obstacle. He quietly lets P6 carry J3 and drops the strict P4. What would show the line was wrong: a case where we "move in Time" with no change of consciousness.

**Catch-alls and gauges.** P9 absorbs any failure to see the machine; the Traveller also names "the Unknown" as where a failed stop sends you. Neither has a gauge — no reading that would show it swallowing J6.

**What the change list leaves out.** It covers direction of travel ("into the future or the past") and "any direction of Space and Time, as the driver determines". It says nothing about *how* the levers act, and the past is never tried. J5 and J6 were added by hearers, not the owner.

**Rivals.** The Medical Man's "sleight-of-hand trick" fits every change on the list. Nothing on the list tells the two apart, so at this level they are the same explanation — which is not a verdict for either.

### 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. A gauge for P9: a reading that differs between a machine that moved in Time and one hidden in the room — then J6 is held.
2. For P8, both halves of a poke: one change that should move the machine, and one that should *not*. If both can be tried, the vanishing becomes evidence; if not, it stays a report.
3. Test the past, where the claim is currently silent.

### 6. What this does not show

These marks are not truth-values. The geometry might be sound while the demonstration is a trick; and real travel might be honest and still fail to convince. Nothing here settles either.

### 7. One next step

Ask for the "would not" half: *name a change to the world that your explanation says would leave the machine unmoved.* The Traveller gives only the half that moves it. Until both halves exist, pressing the lever is a demonstration of something — not yet of travel through Time.
